title: Epic: Port rate limiting from PR#35 to onboarding PR#32
description:
## Why
PR #35 (feat/otp-endpoints) was closed because we moved to OAuth, but it contained a well-designed reusable rate limiting utility (lib/rate-limit.ts) with HMAC-hashed identifiers, sliding-window counting, fail-open/closed controls, and pre-configured limits. PR #32 (onboarding) has several API endpoints that either lack rate limiting entirely or use ad-hoc inline rate limiting (send-invite-email). We need to port the reusable rate-limit module and integrate it into all onboarding endpoints.

## Success Looks Like
1. lib/rate-limit.ts exists on eco-259-fix-tester-feedback-from-v01 branch with the full utility from PR#35
2. Supabase types include rate_limits table
3. All sensitive API endpoints use the shared rate limiter
4. send-invite-email refactored from inline rate limiting to use the shared utility
5. .env.example updated with RATE_LIMIT_HMAC_KEY
6. Build passes (bun run build)

## Scope
- Target branch: eco-259-fix-tester-feedback-from-v01
- Source: origin/feat/otp-endpoints (lib/rate-limit.ts)
- Do NOT port OTP-specific code (email_otps, otp routes, resend email, layer editor changes)
- Only port the generic rate limiting infrastructure and wire it into existing onboarding endpoints

title: Add rate_limits table types to Supabase types
description:
## Files
- app/api/supabase/types.ts (modify)

## What to do
Add the rate_limits table type definitions to the Database type in app/api/supabase/types.ts. The onboarding branch (eco-259-fix-tester-feedback-from-v01) is missing these types even though send-invite-email already writes to rate_limits.

Add inside public.Tables, after purchase_feedback:

```ts
rate_limits: {
  Row: {
    id: string
    identifier: string
    endpoint: string
    created_at: string
  }
  Insert: {
    id?: string
    identifier: string
    endpoint: string
    created_at?: string
  }
  Update: {
    id?: string
    identifier?: string
    endpoint?: string
    created_at?: string
  }
  Relationships: []
}
```

## Don't
- Add email_otps types (that was OTP-specific)
- Change any other table definitions
- Modify the type helper exports at the bottom
acceptance_criteria: 1. rate_limits table type exists in app/api/supabase/types.ts under public.Tables with Row, Insert, Update shapes matching the schema above\n2. No other table definitions are changed\n3. TypeScript compiles without errors (bun run build passes or at minimum tsc --noEmit on this file)

title: Port lib/rate-limit.ts from feat/otp-endpoints branch
acceptance_criteria:
1. lib/rate-limit.ts exists and exports: checkRateLimit, recordRateLimitAttempt, getClientIp, RATE_LIMITS
2. hashIdentifier uses HMAC-SHA256 with RATE_LIMIT_HMAC_KEY env var
3. checkRateLimit has fail-open in dev, fail-closed in production behavior
4. RATE_LIMITS contains entries for: passwordResetRequest, passwordReset, sendInviteEmail, verifyInviteCode, onboard (no OTP entries)
5. .env.example contains RATE_LIMIT_HMAC_KEY
6. File imports only from crypto and @/lib/supabase/server
7. TypeScript compiles without errors
close_reason: 3d23ea5 fix: update RATE_LIMITS config to match spec

title: Refactor send-invite-email to use shared rate limiter
acceptance_criteria:
1. send-invite-email imports checkRateLimit, recordRateLimitAttempt, getClientIp, RATE_LIMITS from @/lib/rate-limit
2. IP-based rate limiting is checked before processing
3. Email-based rate limiting is checked before processing
4. Rate limit attempts are recorded AFTER successful email send (not before)
5. Old inline rate limiting code (manual supabase.from('rate_limits').select/delete/insert) is completely removed
6. 429 responses include Retry-After header and retryAfter in body
7. Invite code generation and email sending logic is unchanged
8. TypeScript compiles without errors
close_reason: c5dafa9 refactor: replace inline rate limiting with shared utility in send-invite-email

title: Add rate limiting to request-password-reset endpoint

4. IP rate limit exceeded returns 429 with Retry-After header
5. Email rate limit exceeded returns 200 (generic success) to prevent enumeration
6. Attempts recorded after successful PDS call
7. Existing PDS proxy logic unchanged
8. TypeScript compiles without errors
